text:
incident-bot: ALERT: decode-stream-prod cohort node decode-12.gpu0 reported >=120 CUDA OOMs in 5m, error 'CUDA out of memory' during decode/stream loop. Node auto-quarantined. Observed streaming request drop rate up to 18% and 503 spike for streaming routes. paging: oncall @Maya.

Maya (oncall): ack, I'm on it. tagging @Liam and @Ashley. beginning triage — can someone paste the last 2m of runtime logs and current routing config?

Liam (sre): seeing repeated failures: stack shows allocation growth in decode step, KV cache size climbs then kernel errors. suspect runaway generation from client side + max_tokens header mismatch. quick check: are we honoring X-Max-Tokens header on the streaming proxy? example header we saw from a client: `X-Max-Tokens: 0` which our SDK interprets as 'no limit' in some older clients.

Ashley (runtime): pasting filtered logs (snip):
```
[21:14:02] decode-12.gpu0 WARN kv_cache.cpp: kv size 1.2GB -> 5.1GB in 30s
[21:14:10] decode-12.gpu0 ERROR decode_loop.cc: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation at step 32768
[21:14:11] decode-12.gpu0 INFO runtime: quarantining node, starting failover
[21:15:30] decode-12.gpu0 INFO model_switcher: routing 40 requests to fallback-cpu-quantized
```
logs show sustained token spiral; a bunch of requests with missing or 0 max_tokens. we have a legacy path where 0 == unlimited.

Liam (sre): that aligns. I think a recent client lib shipped a change so some customers send `max_tokens: 0` to mean 'auto' and our runtime treated that as unbounded. need immediate mitigation: enforce server-side token cap and rate-limit suspect clients, plus route streaming to CPU fallback while we patch.

DevRuntimeBot: Automated action run: `quarantine node decode-12`, `route cohort decode-stream-prod -> fallback-cpu-quantized (3 nodes)`, `enable short-throttle policy per-client 50r/m`, started at 21:16:12 UTC. See run-id: r-1719234567-42.

Carlos (support): customer ops: ticket #7891 from AcmeInc reports 503s and partial responses between 21:12-21:18 UTC. visible to ~120 of their sessions. they're asking if it's a client-side bug or service degradation.

Maya (oncall): mitigation plan (short):
- enforce server max_tokens upper bound of 2000 for all streaming/degenerate values (0 or null treated as 2000)
- enable per-client token quota throttle (50k tokens/10m) for the cohort
- block/flag any requests with `X-Max-Tokens: 0` from older SDKs and return 400 with helpful message until client patch rolls out
- restart decode pool nodes with `--max_tokens-enforce` flag (hotpatch)
- communicate to support: give ETA 30m and workaround (downgrade to non-streaming or set max_tokens explicit small value)

Ashley (runtime): I can hotpatch the runtime binary to interpret 0 as 1 (temporary) and flip the server-side cap. preparing a small config change: `runtime.conf` patch: `max_tokens_server_enforce = 2000` and `treat_zero_max_tokens_as = 2000`. rolling to 10% of decode fleet now.

Liam (sre): also applying a circuit-breaker in the proxy: `if tokens_requested > 2000 -> 429` and `if header X-Max-Tokens == 0 -> tag client and throttle`. I'll push a proxy rule in the next 2m.

Maya (oncall): rolling the changes now. will monitor token throughput and OOM counts. tagging @Eve for customer comms sync.

Eve (prod-ops): noted. I'll draft a short customer advisory: apology, root cause (misinterpreted `max_tokens: 0` -> unbounded), mitigation (server caps and throttles applied), workaround, and ETA for permanent fix.

DevRuntimeBot: Rollout progress: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% of decode fleet patched. All nodes with new config report `max_tokens_enforced=true`. Started at 21:17:10, completed 21:22:05.

Ashley (runtime): restarted quarantine node decode-12 with new flags at 21:22:30. post-restart logs (snip):
```
[21:22:31] decode-12 INFO runtime: max_tokens enforced=2000
[21:22:34] decode-12 INFO decode_loop: normalised incoming request max_tokens=2000 (from 0)
[21:22:40] decode-12 INFO kv_cache: stabilized at 0.9GB
```
OOM counts dropping.

Liam (sre): metrics show request drop rate back down from 18% -> 1.2% and CUDA OOMs falling to baseline. streaming throughput slightly degraded due to fallback routing but stable.

Carlos (support): AcmeInc updated: they confirm degraded UX but mostly recovered after 21:25 UTC. they will push client SDK update to stop sending 0.

Maya (oncall): good. incident severity reduce to mitigated. next: follow-up actions for postmortem and permanent fixes.

Eve (prod-ops): suggest communication plan + timeline:
- send interim note to affected customers in 2h with current impact and steps taken
- postmortem doc due EOD tomorrow
- prioritize SDK patch compatibility check (+server tests) for next sprint

Ashley (runtime): follow-ups I will own:
- PR to runtime to treat 0 as invalid and require explicit max_tokens or server-default.
- add unit/regression test for header misinterpretation.
- add telemetry to flag clients that send 0 for 30d.

Liam (sre): follow-ups I will own:
- proxy rule permanent: drop/400 for weird values, metric alarm on token-per-request 99p shift
- runbook update for decode OOM: include token-cap enforcement and fallback routing steps

Maya (oncall): support actions:
- Carlos to send customer advisory draft and list of affected tenants
- escalate to SEs for any enterprise contracts impacted

Carlos (support): noted. will open a customer escalation bundle and attach telemetry and correlation to ticket #7891.

Maya (oncall): tl;dr: root cause = misinterpreted `max_tokens=0` from some client SDKs -> server allowed effectively unbounded generation -> KV cache growth -> CUDA OOMs -> node quarantines -> request drops. mitigation = server-side cap (2000), proxy rate-limits, fallback routing, node restart with hotpatch. incident closed as mitigated; postmortem + action items assigned. :white_check_mark: :warning:

DevRuntimeBot: Incident run summary: id=r-1719234567-42, start=21:14 UTC, mitigated=21:25 UTC, actions taken=[quarantine node, route to fallback, enforce server caps, proxy rules, fleet hotpatch].

Maya (oncall): leaving final note — please add any more items or edits. I'll hand this to the postmortem writer in 30m.

Eve (prod-ops): thanks all. assigning postmortem owner: Ashley. closing thread for paging but keep this thread for notes.
